rows.doi_or_pmid: doi:10.1016/j.dsi.2018.04.008; PMID not in saved text
rows.design: uncontrolled case series: 4 patients treated, reported one by one (one row per patient and time point); no comparator; a 5th patient had histochemistry only; histochemistry of lesional versus normal skin (Table 1) is a separate mechanism endpoint, not a treatment endpoint, and is not extracted as a row
rows.skin_tone: not reported [Tokyo clinic; the Discussion's 'Caucasoid versus Mongoloid' contrast suggests East Asian patients, but the patients' skin type or ancestry is not stated]
rows.patients_enrolled: 5 ('All the 5 patients'); [4] treated ('Four of ﬁve patients underwent this treatment'); one had histochemistry only ('One of ﬁve patients underwent histochemical testes only')
rows.analysis_unit: patient (single case; results are narrative for the patient's grafted macules as a whole, no per-macule count)
rows.intervention: mini-punch grafting using a machine (mMG): punches 0.8-1.0 mm wide, 1.8 mm deep removed from the lesion with an electric micro drill; donor punches 0.8-1.0 mm wide, 1.5 mm deep from scalp without hair follicles placed into the holes; then NB-UVB 311 nm, 2 MED, to all grafts from 1 week after grafting, three times a week for 1-2 months
rows.comparator: none (no untreated, NB-UVB-only or graft-only macules)
rows.endpoint_definition: author-described repigmentation of the grafted macules ('excellent color-matched repigmentation', 'long-lasting repigmentation'); not defined, no grade or percentage
rows.assessment_method: clinical observation with photographs (Fig. 1) by the treating clinic [assessor not named]; no scale, no instrument, no blinding, no independent assessor
rows.texture_or_scar: not reported [the Methods say shallower donor punches were used so 'the graft and recipient lesional skin go ﬂat'; no scar, cobblestoning or texture outcome is reported]
rows.attrition: 1 of the [4] treated patients (45-year-old woman) 'did not visit our clinic after this time' (after 1 month); the others were followed to 5 (72-year-old man), 8 (11-year-old boy) and 12 (46-year-old man) months [all timed from mMG]
rows.citation: Hirobe T, Enami H. Melanoblasts but not melanocytes decrease in number in human epidermis of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis. Dermatol Sin 2018;36:131-135
rows.diagnosis: IGH (HE histology reported: 'These observations strongly suggest that this disease is IGH')
rows.body_site: back (72-year-old man; macules 'increased in number for two years')
rows.lesions_enrolled: approximately 120 macules, 3 mm in diameter; 120 grafts transplanted
rows.source_location: Results, Skin grafting, first paragraph; Fig. 1A, E
rows.time_from_last_treatment: NOT_DERIVABLE: the paper gives 2 months after mMG (grafting); NB-UVB started 'After 1 week' and continued 'three times a week for 1e2 months', end date per patient not reported [between before the final NB-UVB exposure and about 1 month after it]
rows.arm_result: minigrafts 'survived after 4 days'; 'excellent color-matched repigmentation was observed after 2 months' (no extent or count given)
rows.complete_match: [author's claim only] 'excellent color-matched repigmentation' by eye; extent of coverage not reported, no measure
rows.uncertainty: Uncontrolled case series of 4 treated patients by the treating clinic; no comparator, so the effect of the grafts cannot be separated from the NB-UVB course given to every graft. Every time point is counted from grafting (Fig. 1 captions: 'months after mMG'), not from the final treatment: NB-UVB began 'After 1 week' and continued 'three times a week for 1e2 months', and the end date for each patient is not reported, so months after the final treatment are NOT_DERIVABLE; it is also not stated whether the 1-2 months run from grafting or from the first exposure. The Discussion speaks of 'NB-UVB irradiations before and after the grafting', but the Methods describe NB-UVB only after grafting; any pre-graft course is not described (internal contradiction). Repigmentation and colour match are the authors' own visual judgement: no grading scale, percentage, assessor, blinding or instrument; extent of coverage of each macule and the number of macules that repigmented are not reported; the claim that 'all grafts' and 'all IGH macules treated' repigmented rests on these four narrative cases. The Discussion says repigmentation appeared 'after 1e2 months', and the 72-year-old man is reported at 2 months, the others at 1 month. Durability is author-stated for one patient each at 8 months (11-year-old boy) and 12 months (46-year-old man) after grafting, with no measure; [if NB-UVB ended 1 to 2.25 months after grafting, these are about 5.75 to 7 and 9.75 to 11 months after the last exposure], so the 8-month case may fall short of six months after the final treatment. Falabella et al. (ref 21), cited here, reported minigrafts in IGH becoming depigmented 18 months after grafting, a later point than any follow-up in this paper. The 72-year-old man was 'followed up until 5 months' but his result is stated only at 4 months. Diagnosis: HE histology is reported for the 72-year-old man's macules ('These observations strongly suggest that this disease is IGH'); for the others the diagnostic basis is not stated, though histochemistry was done on lesional skin of all five (Table 1). An IGH patient aged 11 is unusual for the disease as the Introduction describes it ('usually affects aged humans over 50e60 years'). Adverse effects, donor-site outcome, and darkening are not reported. Macule size 'approximately 3 mm in diameter'; the authors credit the small size for the speed of repigmentation. Fig. 3 caption calls patient 1C's samples 'normal leg skin' and 'lesional leg skin', while the Results place this 46-year-old man's macules on his left arm and panel C says 'normal arm epidermis' (internal inconsistency in the figure legend). Table 1 (not extracted as rows; mechanism data, a Module 5 lead): lesional melanocytes 104.7 ± 9.7% of normal, melanoblasts 28.9 ± 4.6%, three punch biopsies per site in each of 5 patients; the 54-year-old man in Table 1 does not appear in Fig. 1 and is [the histochemistry-only patient]. Table 1 was read from the PDF text in column order; its row and column assignment is clear from the order but was not checked against the printed page image. Same authors and technique as their vitiligo mMG paper (ref 8, doi:10.1016/j.dsi.2018.01.004). The saved text renders en dashes as 'e' (for example '1e2 months') and keeps ligature characters, as pdftotext produced them.
